title: A skip link or landmarks let you go past the navigation bar
note: The first Tab did not expose a usable skip link in this run. Chromium’s accessibility tree exposed a main landmark after the header.

title: All navigation bar items work with the keyboard
note: The header brand and Catalog, Registration and Student Profile navigation items were keyboard reachable. Enter opened the corresponding views.

title: Search and all filters work with the keyboard
note: Typing “computer” worked in #catalog-search. Arrow Down changed 5 dropdowns, including #filter-department.

title: You can fill in and submit the registration form with the keyboard
note: Tab, arrow keys and Space as applicable let me complete #registration-form. Enter opened #confirmation-modal.

title: Course card buttons and table buttons (register / drop) work with the keyboard
note: Enter activated the catalog “Details” action and the Registration table “Drop” action.

title: The focus does not get stuck anywhere on the page
note: Forward and reverse Tab reached controls before and after the catalog filters, registration fields and course tables. Dialog confinement was checked under M2.

title: The focus order follows the visual order
note: At 1280 px, tabbing followed the header, then the visible controls in the Catalog, Registration and Student Profile reading order.

title: The focus is always visible
note: The focus indicator for “Register” in Catalog disappeared behind the sticky header during keyboard navigation.

title: The focused element is not hidden behind other content
note: The sticky header covered part or all of the focused “Register” control in Catalog during keyboard navigation.

title: The focus goes into the modal when it opens
note: Opening #confirmation-modal placed keyboard focus on #btn-close-confirm-modal inside the dialog.

title: Tab and Shift+Tab stay in the modal while it is open
note: Tab and Shift+Tab moved among the controls in #confirmation-modal.

title: Esc and the close or cancel button close the modal
note: Escape and the Cancel or Close button both dismissed #confirmation-modal.

title: The focus goes back to the button that opened the modal
note: Escape and the Close or Cancel control in #confirmation-modal returned focus to #btn-submit-registration.

title: VoiceOver says that a dialog opened and reads its name
note: NVDA announced “Confirm Course Registration” as a dialog on opening. Chromium inspection confirmed its modal role, title reference and explicit aria-modal="true".

title: Each field has a visible label and VoiceOver reads it
note: Visible Registration labels are associated with their fields in #registration-form, including #reg-course-select. NVDA spoke “Course Registration and Enrollment” on #reg-course-select.

title: Required fields are marked with text or a symbol that is explained (not color only)
note: #reg-course-select is required in Registration. The form lacks an explanation for the required-field markings.

title: An empty or wrong submit shows each error in text next to its field
note: The toast and announcer requested a course selection, but no inline message appeared next to #reg-course-select.

title: Each error message tells how to correct it
note: The corrective instruction was available only in the temporary toast after submit.

title: VoiceOver reads the errors after submit
note: Focus moved to #reg-course-select, and NVDA announced the course-selection error.

title: VoiceOver reads the result count after a search or filter change and the focus stays in place
note: NVDA announced “Showing 3 of 16 courses” during the catalog search or filter check. Typing “computer” left focus on #catalog-search.

title: VoiceOver reads the confirmation after you register or drop a course
note: NVDA announced the course-specific success messages after both registering and dropping. Each message was delivered through the live region observed in Chromium.

title: Each page or view has a title that tells what it is
note: Home, Catalog, Registration and Student Profile all retained the title “Apex University | Course Registration System”. NVDA’s title command read the Catalog title as “Apex University Course Registration System”.

title: Headings: one h1 per view and levels in a logical order
note: Catalog jumps from “Course Catalog & Schedule” (h1) to course titles marked h3. NVDA read the sampled catalog heading levels in browse mode.

title: Landmarks: banner or header and navigation and main and footer
note: Chromium exposed banner, main navigation, main content and contentinfo landmarks in each view. NVDA landmark navigation announced main, content info.

title: Link and button names tell what they do
note: Catalog action names include the specific course code or title in Chromium’s accessibility tree. NVDA read different course-specific names for the two sampled details controls.

title: Meaningful images and icons have a text alternative and decorative ones are hidden
note: Decorative header and course-card SVGs and icons were hidden from the Chromium accessibility tree. Adjacent text supplied the visible control labels. NVDA’s graphic shortcut from the top of Catalog found no announced graphic.

title: VoiceOver reads the column header for each cell of the registered-courses table
note: The registered-courses table identifies “COURSE CODE” and its other column headers with th scope="col". NVDA announced column information while moving across the sampled registered-courses table cells.

title: Dropdowns and toggles and tabs announce their role and state (for example expanded or selected)
note: #theme-toggle changes the theme without exposing a pressed state. NVDA announced “collapsed” and “expanded” for the mobile menu.

title: The navigation bar tells which page is the current page
note: The header marked the selected Home, Catalog, Registration and Student Profile item with aria-current="page".

title: At 320 px width there is no horizontal scroll and no content is lost
note: At 320 × 568 px, the header action group and the registration layout extended past the page edge. In Registration, the document measured 642 px wide in a 305 px content viewport.

title: At 200% zoom all text is readable and nothing is cut off or on top of other content
note: At actual 200% Chrome zoom, Registration headings, fields and table text remained readable. The registered-courses table could be scrolled within its own container.

title: Errors and status and selected filters are not shown by color only
note: Availability and errors include explicit text, filters show the selected option, and the active navigation has an underline or weight cue.

title: Focus indicators and field borders have a contrast of at least 3:1
note: The #catalog-search field border (#e2e8f0) measured 1.23:1 against #ffffff, below 3:1.

title: The needs-review contrast sample passes (4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text)
note: The Catalog Waitlist badge measured 2.86:1 (#d97706 on #fef3c7), below 4.5:1.
